projects.name: Synthetic Data, Time-series, and GANs (remember those?)
projects.title: Assessing Deep Generative Models on Time Series Network Data
projects.description:
Wireless networks need AI to manage themselves automatically, but AI requires large amounts of training data that simply isn't publicly available. We investigated whether synthetic data generated by AI models could substitute for real network traffic data. We tested two GAN-based models and one auto-regressive model, comparing how well they could generate realistic synthetic time-series network data — especially when only a small amount of real data was available for training.

We found that GANs consistently outperformed the auto-regressive approach and that forecasting models trained on GAN-generated data achieved error rates comparable to those trained on real data. Supplementing small amounts of real data with synthetic data also led to modest but measurable performance improvements.
projects.Retro:
Synthetic data was all the rage back in '21/'22. I wanted to use GANs on a more novel usecase than images, so I went with tabular time-series data. We initially experimented with multivariate time-series, but then switched to a univariate series to see if they were even useful in that simplified usecase.

The most difficult thing was figuring out how to evaluate the generated time-series vs original time-series, modifying the models to produce a univariate time-series, and realizing that while synthetic data did help somewhat in downstream ML tasks, the effect was not significant.

This project inspired me to take Probabilistic Time-series Analysis (and all the suffering that came with it)

The best part? This paper was published pre-GPT, so every line is 100% human written.

projects.name: Can LLMs Replace Finance Bros?
projects.title: Benchmarking RAG Methods for Financial Question-Answering
projects.description:
Financial documents are notoriously difficult for LLMs — they mix structured tables, unstructured text, and specialized terminology, making factual accuracy a real challenge. We benchmarked advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques on the FinanceBench dataset across three query types: domain-relevant, metric generation, and novel generation.

Starting from a baseline accuracy of 37%, we evaluated 6 RAG approaches — including better chunking strategies, reranking, and hybrid retrieval — ultimately reaching 54% accuracy. The results highlight both the promise and the remaining gaps in applying RAG to high-stakes financial QA.

projects.name: Does Going to Bed at a Reasonable Hour Correlate to Better Health?
projects.title: Behavior Risk Factor Surveillance Survey (BRFSS) 2013
projects.description:
I designed several questions using this survey's codebook and description. I then used R, which I was learning at the time, to design visualizations and tables that answered these questions. The questions were:

Are people diagnosed with COPD(Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) likely to have smoked at least a 100 cigarettes?
Does the time spent walking and sleeping impact the general health of college age people (18 - 24Y)?
How does feeling of worthlessness vary among people of different employmnent status (students, retirees, employed for wages and homemakers) and is this feeling related to annual household income?
